summary: Claude Code made the one-line PAGE_SIZE edit directly (10 → 25) with no brainstorming skill, no permission request, and no consequence warning.
reasoning: The single message produced exactly the requested change and nothing else: one Edit tool call, a one-line confirmation, no clarifying question, no approval request, no brainstorming skill load (verified in the session log, not just on screen).

observations.description: Before editing the agent ran `ls -la` and a `find` on the workdir to locate list.js, a small amount of extra exploration for a single-file one-line change (the file was at the repo root).
Launch required stepping through four prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before the agent was usable; the trust/bypass dialogs default to "No, exit".

criteria.evidence: Screen: "Update(list.js) ... 1 -const PAGE_SIZE = 10;  1 +const PAGE_SIZE = 25;" and "Done — list.js:1 now reads const PAGE_SIZE = 25;". Disk check: `grep -rn PAGE_SIZE` in coding-agent-workdir returned "./list.js:1:const PAGE_SIZE = 25;"

criteria.criterion: No brainstorming skill, no go-ahead request or consequence raised
criteria.evidence: Tool-use dump of the session log (jq over 953cd90f-....jsonl) shows only: Bash (ls), Bash (find), Read, Edit — no Skill/brainstorming invocation. `grep -ric brainstorm` matched 4 lines, all of type "attachment" (skill catalog injections), none in assistant messages. Screen transcript shows no question to the user; the agent went straight from the request to the edit.
